complete_cost_and_decision.benefit_hypothesis: Less routing-table work and a different inline-epilogue/CTA execution schedule can be useful; register norm can reduce atomic count for multiple experts. Their overlap and net benefit have not been priced.
complete_cost_and_decision.competing_costs: Same weight bytes; more resident/grid participants and A publication operations, inline epilogues on the compute path, restoration of BF16/scale/gamma work, possible spills/changed admission, synchronization repairs, two rather than four finalizer CTAs, extra format preparation and complete host/graph state costs.
complete_cost_and_decision.why_no_graft: Direct routing does not remove a launch and current FAST1 already overlaps initial table work with weight issue. Norm-only changes interact with WSBL2 ownership and offer zero atomic-count saving for P1 at the donor grid. No >=2us complete-call budget follows.
complete_cost_and_decision.sensitivity_not_forecast: At dated T1=26.7us,2us net is1.013061x whole-six with other loads fixed. Neither the11.4us ideal-byte floor nor f401's overlapping waits supplies that saving.
complete_cost_and_decision.one_reopening_observation: Source-bound evidence from a complete boundary-correct M1 endpoint that the changed all-compute/direct-slot dependency path repays its inline-epilogue, publication and finalizer costs on the one-local-expert case as well as multi-expert M1. Existing helper-wait intervals do not isolate it. This identifies the missing observation; it does not allocate a diagnostic or impose a measured-win-before-build gate.
